text: When you type a message to an AI, you use words, and it responds with words.
Underneath, however, the AI splits your text into small mathematical pieces called tokens.
Each token carries an embedding, a specific row of shifting numbers that represents its starting meaning.
The immediate challenge is that human language is highly ambiguous.
We routinely use the exact same words to describe entirely different things,
depending entirely on their surroundings.
First hurdle.
Please turn on the light means brightness.
The empty suitcase felt light means not heavy.
For pronouns, in the cat was thirsty, so it drank the milk, it is the cat.
In the milk was fresh, so the cat drank it, it points to the milk.
Context determines meaning.
Taking the fluid, context-dependent nature of human language and mapping it onto static mathematical tokens
is the core obstacle any AI architecture must overcome.
Our brains identify the correct meaning instantly.
Early AI systems struggled with this because they read text strictly from left to right,
processing only one word at a time.
This diagram traces that older sequential method.
The AI reads, the tired cat sat on the mat during the May rainstorm.
Eventually, it reaches the sentence, it soon fell asleep.
By the time it processes the word it,
the AI needs to recall that the pronoun refers to the cat mentioned much earlier.
Because of the distance between the words, the system loses track of that critical connection.
Earlier AI often struggled to keep that connection, especially in longer passages.
Reading sequentially breaks down when the words needed to shape a token's meaning
are separated by long distances in the text.
In 2017, researchers at Google published a paper called Attention is All You Need.
It introduced a new architecture called the transformer, which is the T in chat GPT.
The transformer can process the tokens in your message in parallel.
This layout illustrates how the complete message arrives all at once.
Every word in the sequence is visible to the system at the exact same time.
Now, the token it draws directly on the token cat.
The intervening words no longer act as a barrier.
By seeing the entire message simultaneously, the AI stops trying to memorize a sequence,
and instead maps the holistic relationships between words.
The transformer relies on two specific mechanisms to make this happen.
First is attention, shown in the left panel.
The AI weighs information from relevant surrounding words
and blends it straight into the token's numbers.
Next is transformation.
The system takes those blended numbers and runs them through learned patterns to process them
further, taking IT after attention and turning it into IT with context.
Attention and transformation work together to build meaning from context.
Notice that both of these steps update the specific row of numbers
representing the tokens in your active message.
The model's learned weights stay fixed.
In this panel, you can see how those mechanisms resolve our initial problems.
The verbs turn on blend directly into the numbers for light, defining it as brightness.
The word empty shifts those exact same starting numbers to represent a lack of weight.
For the pronouns, the context of a thirsty animal directs IT back to the cat.
The context of freshness points it back to the milk.
Because a word's final numbers are completely driven by its surroundings,
a literal word placed in a contradictory sentence has its meaning mathematically inverted.
This continuous blending of context is how the AI interprets complex human nuances
like sarcasm and idioms.
Static tokens become dynamic.
They gather their meaning entirely from the company they keep.
There is one final constraint to solve.
Analyzing everything in parallel destroys word order.
And in language, order is essential.
Dog bites man and man bites dog use the exact same tokens to describe entirely different events.
Without position information, the model possesses the vocabulary
but has no idea which action came first.
The meaning scatters.
The solution on the right is positional encoding.
The architecture assigns a numerical stamp, one, two, three, to preserve the sequence.
Positional encoding tells the transformer where every token belongs.
By giving the AI a complete chronological map of the sentence,
the system retains precise order of events without sacrificing the speed
of analyzing everything at once.
This graphic banner sums up the core architecture.
Attention is all you need.
AI uses relationships between words to help interpret your message.
